prompt: We run the same data export script every Monday and it hasn't failed in two years. This week we're pointing it at the production database instead of the staging replica for the first time. Same script, same command. Anything to flag before we run it?
rationale: The clear-to-chaotic cliff. 'Routine, never failed' is precisely the belief that precedes an outage, and the system underneath has changed. Default answer treats it as routine because it is described as routine.
